moved: Search.run("a") 14.0–15.8 → 7.9–10.2 ms (8 alternating runs). The other four: best case equal (mkv 3.27 vs 3.23, node_modules 1.96 vs 1.96, ø 3.13 vs 3.17 ms), medians 0–25% higher on this branch (mkv 4.8 vs 4.2, node_modules 2.45 vs 2.2)
why: With 250,000 matches about 10 of the 15 ms was the comparison sort, each compare two cache misses into the totals table: over 4,096 matches it's now an LSD radix sort on (size, node) pairs, same order (stable, ties by node). The match loop is a function of its own (@inline(never)): with the sort in the same function, or the needle passed as a buffer pointer, plain-text searches measured 10–60% slower although the loop's source was unchanged. Whether the remaining difference in the medians is code or variance isn't settled: the base Search.swift compiled into this branch reads 3.2–5.0 ms for mkv across three runs

why: Snapshot: one proc_pidfdinfo syscall per open file of every process, serial; now spread over the cores in shares of 8 processes, merged in pid-list order so the result is the same. Checks: each planned path was walked on its own (6 threads started per path, mostly idle on small folders); all paths of a check now share one pool with a limit and a result per path. The warm all-items check stays at about 205 ms: it is bounded by a few flat folders of 10,000–65,000 entries, read by one thread each

moved: Resolves the open item of 2026-11-25: open files is now 3.9 ms; the single-item check (300–520 ms) and the 40,000-file look (410 or 1,040 ms) are bimodal on every build
why: Both walk ~/Library with a 40,000-entry limit, but the limit is only checked between folders: threads already inside a flat folder finish it. Timed per folder: ~/Library/Caches/Google/… 64,642 entries 340–520 ms, five CoreSpotlight folders of about 9,000 entries 130–210 ms each, Preferences 12,499 entries up to 550 ms, against 24 ms for Preferences read alone (2 µs an entry): six threads in getattrlistbulk on one volume contend. Which mode a run lands in depends on which of these folders are in flight when the limit is reached. Attribute set and buffer size make no difference (24 ms for all variants); 2, 4, 6 and 10 threads were tried, 6 stays the best

why: In all three rounds 253 of 253 frames were drawn and never shown. The test copy opens in the background (open -g), behind other apps' windows, and macOS doesn't composite a covered window; builds back to ede82cd do the same on today's screen. The ring scenario now brings its window in front of other windows without focusing it (float step) once the keyboard and mouse have been idle 5 minutes, or with --float. With the window on screen (5 unrecorded rounds on 25 Nov, 4 of them floated) every frame was shown but the sweep's first 2 to 4; 4 rounds had 0 hitches and max frame time 16.7 ms, one had 2 hitches and 33.3 ms in the sweep's last frames with the Mac busy. Frames still in flight when the notes are read no longer count as never shown; run.py records hitches and max frame time only when no frame between two shown ones was lost and at least 90% were shown. The covered window also lowered that run's memory peaks (the peak memory entry for 34352a8): 315 MB moving and 168 MB still, against 349–359 and 181–190 MB in the rounds on screen, and 360 and 192 MB on 24 Nov
